name: Calcium (total)
rangeNote: About half of the calcium in blood is carried by albumin, a blood protein. When albumin is low, total calcium reads low even if the active (free) calcium is normal, so the result is read together with albumin. Some labs also report a corrected calcium or measure the free (ionised) calcium directly.
summary: Calcium keeps bones and teeth strong and is needed for nerves, muscles and the heart to work. This test measures all the calcium in blood: the part attached to proteins and the free, active part. The body keeps it in a narrow range.

high.meaning: A mildly high calcium often causes no symptoms. Higher levels can cause thirst, passing a lot of urine, constipation, tiredness and confusion. Lasting high calcium is most often from an overactive parathyroid gland or, less often, cancer, and needs a doctor to find the cause.
commonCauses: Large amounts of calcium, vitamin D or vitamin A supplements
Water pills (thiazide diuretics) and some other medicines
Dehydration or a tight tourniquet during the blood draw

low.meaning: A low total calcium often just reflects a low albumin, the protein that carries much of it. A truly low calcium can cause tingling around the mouth or in the fingers, muscle cramps and, when severe, heart rhythm problems.
commonCauses: Low albumin (the active calcium may still be normal)
After neck surgery on the thyroid or parathyroid glands
Some bone medicines, such as denosumab or bisphosphonate infusions
